subject: Small sample size issue in SEM with binary response variable

messages.author: cddfc3fb21fe9046
messages.subject: Small sample size issue in SEM with binary response variable
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to use SEM in an ecological context (cfr. Frauendorf et al. 2021 https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2656.13578). More specifically I use SEM to construct an overall condition index for the great tit, a bird species. Using CFA, I summarize all my morphological and physiological measurements into 6 latent variables (energy stores, nutritional condition, pre- and post-fledging developmental stress, aging and hormonal stress). Together they make up the composite variable 'overall condition' (cond) which is regressed over my response variable 'tick01' to answer my research question if birds in better condition have a lower chance to be infected by a tick. Since tick01 is binary, I define it as ordered and use the estimator WLSMV.

Questions:

1) Due to the addition of variable CORT2 (defining HS) to the model, the sample size is strongly reduced (from 202 to 96). However HS seems to have a highly significant contribution to the composite variable 'cond' and therefore I do not want to exclude this from the model. Since the WLSMV estimator requires a minimum sample size of 200, how do I best cope with this small sample size? Adding complete.cases / bootstrapping / Bayesian approach like blavaan?

2) The regression tick01 ~ cond gives a std.all of 1.054. Is this due to the small sample size? Is this a problem in interpreting the results?

2) My model gives a negative error variance for my response variable tick01 (-0.109) and a NA for its R-square. Is this problematic? If so, how to solve this?

3) I receive warning messages that the observed variables defining ES are strongly correlated (nearly 1). They are also strongly correlated to tick01. What do I have to add to my model to correct for this?

Many thanks in advance. I am happy to deliver all extra information needed.

Best,
Bram

messages.author: 08e48595b188026f
messages.subject: Re: Small sample size issue in SEM with binary response variable
parts:
Hi Bram,

I am not familiar with the topic, but from the statistical point of view, I can make the following observations:
1.You might try to use missing = "pairwise" to include units with missing values.
2. & 2. (you have bullet 2. twice). This would indicate a haywood case i.e., there is something wrong with the estimation model. There are no simple answers here. You have to figure out why this occurs (e.g., try removing the variables and changing the model to see what configuration produces this and then try to interpret why this is the case). The best option here is probably to modify the model (based on theory). Larger sample might help, but that is probably hard to do.
3. Not sure if the warning about the correlation is about the manifest or estimated covariances. Either way, you probably have a problem of multicollinearity and you might try to remove redundant variables. (i.e., if there is a correlation of 1, then they represent the same facet).

Additional observations:
a. You model cond as a composite/formative variable. But is it identified? See e.g. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusres.2008.01.009, specifically section 5.3.3.
b. In case of ES variable, why did you set variances of manifest variables to 0? Why do you regress residualBM on wings, tail, tarsus length? Maybe you could obtain the residualBM in another analysis (e.g., regression analysis) and then use only the residuals in this analysis. Would probably simplify the model.

The bottom line is that you should not interpret the results of the current model. Revisions are needed.

Hope my comments help at least a bit!
Best,
Jošt
